about: Browser mission of 2026-11-17 (UTC; the flight after the presentation sweep, sub-wave 3.2: the app on createSession): tests/browser/mission/lunar-direct.spec.ts, one flight, pad to splashdown, flown by the test pilot in the page through the controls. The windows and the phase log of the full record (out/mission/browser-mission.json) are left out here; `windowsOverTheLines` and `comparison` are computed from them and from browser-mission-2026-11-12.json.

pictureComparison.how: Every picture of this flight was looked at beside the picture of the same name of 2026-11-12 (the old set copied aside before the run), old left and new right at 960 x 540 each; the splash pictures and seven others at that size singly, the rest on sheets at half of it. Beside that, for every pair: the mean difference of the two pictures, the share of each HUD panel that changed strongly (text that changed its words, a panel that appeared or went), and the pictures' numbers of the two records (altitude, EV100, mean luminance, bodies in the frame, the sound buses' levels).

samePicture.pictures: 00-pad to 07-tli-complete (15 pictures: the pad, lift-off, max Q, the three of each stage separation and of the fairing, Earth orbit from outside and from the couch, TLI complete)
samePicture.finding: The same pictures: the same frame of the same flight (identical milestone records through EARTH_ORBIT, identical time of TLI_COMPLETE), mean difference 0.3 to 4.3 of 255, no HUD panel changed (0.0 % strongly changed in the left, right and bottom panels; 0 to 1.8 % at the top centre, where a toast is caught at another moment of its fade). The max-Q picture is one frame later (14 881 m against 14 878 m).

sameSceneClosedLoop.finding: The same scenes with the differences of a flight that is closed-loop after the parking orbit: times 1 to 3 s apart (50 s at the Moon's sphere of influence on the way back), attitudes and headings a few degrees apart, numbers in the panels a few units apart in the last digits. Framing, effects and words as on 2026-11-12: the RCS puffs in lunar orbit, the lander's shadow converging in the descent, the cabin on the Moon, the plasma sheath and wake at the peak of the heating, the white-out at the peak of the load, the capsule under its risers in the low sun. Mean difference 0.3 to 9.0; HUD panels 0 to 1.1 % (left and right), up to 3.9 % at the bottom (the navball turned by the other heading).

differs.what: From one second after the splash on the foam round the capsule is smaller and dimmer, and at +10 s and +34 s it is a faint grey trace where 2026-11-12 had a wide pink-white patch; the sea round the capsule reads black; mean luminance 96 against 126 at +1 s, 51 against 88 at +3 s, 44 against 59 at +10 s, 49 against 60 at the milestone, with the same EV100 from +3 s on (11.7, 11.1, 11.0). The meter stops down sooner (EV100 11.7 at +1 s against 9.3). The canopy comes down nearer to the camera and stands larger in the frame.
differs.why: Not the sweep. (1) The ocean's own change of 2026-11-16, before the sweep (commit cff94bd, 'the black sea after the splashdown ... taken apart'): a hull churns wake foam by its speed through the water, not by the time it lies in it, so a capsule at rest no longer keeps a wide patch alive. (2) The known fault of the meter stopping down while the sunlit canopies stand in the frame (request ocean-13), with a canopy that fell nearer the camera in this flight.

differs.what: The status line 'TEST PILOT - splashdown' is gone and the toast 'Test pilot finished' fades in under 'Splashdown': the pilot had finished when the milestone was recorded (the phase at the milestone is 'done', it was 'splashdown').
differs.why: The order of two things that happen within a frame or two of each other at the end of the flight; nothing is missing.

differs.what: The record now names the Moon as the body in the frame; on 2026-11-12 it named none.
differs.why: The app's own correction after that flight (bodiesInFrame below a body's reference radius), confirmed in a browser by this flight: none of the seven 'no body in the frame' failures of 2026-11-12 came back.

pictureComparison.sound: At no picture is a sound bus silent that was heard on 2026-11-12, or heard that was silent (engines, aero, reentry, events, cabin, ui, master; levels at the instant of the picture). The largest differences in level: the aero bus at +10 s after the splash (rms 0.003 then, 0.031 now) and the events bus at the fairing jettison (0.0036 then, 0.0007 now): the sound runs on in real time while the simulation stands at a stop, so the instant caught differs.
pictureComparison.newAndWrong: Nothing that the pictures show is new and wrong since 2026-11-12. The known faults are all still there (the ribbons in the sea's glint at max Q, the grey panes with the Sun or the plasma in them, no dust or plume at the lunar landing and lift-off, the white-out at the peak of the load, the canopies above the frame under the chutes and as flat fans on the water, the meter stopping down after the splash, the box-shaped dark patch in front of the floating capsule).

notes.tree: HEAD 55dd2d1 (the presentation sweep, sub-wave 3.2, complete: the app on createSession / LocalSession); the flight ran 2026-11-17 09:59-10:45 PST, alone in the GPU slot, with other work on the machine (the sweep's reviewer) in its first half hour.
notes.identicalAndMoved: LIFTOFF, MAX_Q, STAGE_SEP_1, FAIRING_JETTISON, STAGE_SEP_2 and EARTH_ORBIT: the time and every field of the milestone record identical to 2026-11-12 (38, 41, 38, 34, 32 and 35 fields). TLI_COMPLETE: the time identical, 15 of 32 fields identical, the others moved in the fifth to eighth digit (altitude -0.08 m, mass -0.025 kg, the predicted time of the Moon's sphere of influence -11.6 s). From MOON_SOI_ENTER on the flight is closed-loop: the times moved by +2.0 s (sphere of influence), +2.5 s (lunar orbit), +1.7 s (touchdown and lift-off), -50.3 s (leaving the sphere of influence, perigee targeted), -1.4 to -1.1 s (entry interface to splashdown); see comparison.milestones for every field.
notes.frameIntervalLine: As flown the line failed in three phases: prelaunch, ignition, moonArrival. (1) prelaunch: one interval of 166.7 ms at index 0 of the first window after the pad's picture, with a slowest frame of 6.0 ms and the render core's largest frame-to-frame time of 17.3 ms in that window: the stall of the spec's own screenshot, which ended after the window was started. The spec now lets two frames pass after its pictures before it starts a window (two part flights to MAX_Q afterwards: 2071 intervals on the pad, the longest 16.9 ms). Not a frame the game dropped. (2) ignition: one interval of 33.3 ms in 181 frames (0.55 %; line 0.5 %): the lift-off frame, 24.1 ms on the main thread (simulation 11.2, render 10.6 with the terrain's hooks 5.2), missed one display frame. On 2026-11-12 the same phase failed on the same frame. (3) moonArrival: one frame of 466.7 ms: sky.prepare 474.8 ms in the frame the Moon's sphere of influence is entered (452 ms on 2026-11-12, then without a breakdown). The sky package's.
notes.mainThread: 10 phases over 6 ms p99 (6 on 2026-11-12). The six of 2026-11-12 again (ignition, vertical, pitchProgramme, m1Separation, terminal, touchdown (cockpit)) and mcc1:trim 6.54, approach 6.59, touchdown 7.12, lunarAscent 6.09. The machine was busier in the first half hour of this flight and quieter in the last ten minutes than on 2026-11-12: the phases' medians are 1.0 to 1.4 ms higher from the pad to the lunar surface (prelaunch 3.17 to 4.18, parkingCoast 1.89 to 2.81, surface 2.76 to 4.16) and 1.0 to 1.6 ms LOWER from the trans-Earth coast to the splashdown (transEarth 3.80 to 2.16, entry 3.39 to 2.39, splashdown 3.78 to 2.69). A part flight to MAX_Q an hour later read 2.62 ms on the pad (p99 4.58), under 2026-11-12. What is higher in every phase, loaded or not, is the simulation stage: p99 0.92 to 1.09 ms in the splashdown phase, 0.91 to 1.04 in the entry, 0.56 to 0.65 on the pad: about 0.1 to 0.2 ms for the session over the simulation.
notes.appSuite: tests/browser/app before the flight (09:42-09:58 PST): functional 10 of 10; perf 2 of 3: the 1440p climb's main thread 6.20 ms p99 (line 6; 5.41 on 2026-11-12), on the busy machine (medians 0.7 to 1.2 ms above 2026-11-12 at every checkpoint); the frame-interval line held at all seven checkpoints.
